learningObjectives: Split datasets into training, validation, and test sets appropriately.
Select evaluation metrics based on the machine learning problem.
Identify overfitting and underfitting using model behavior.

activities.title: Build the Data Split
activities.instruction: Arrange the roles of the training, validation, and test sets.

content.concept: Training data is used to fit a model, validation data supports model selection and tuning, and test data provides a final estimate using unseen data.
content.tip: Interact with the example first. Your progress is saved for this session.

activities.title: Match Evaluation Metrics
activities.instruction: Match each metric with the type of performance it measures.

content.concept: Different metrics capture different aspects of classification and regression performance, so the metric should match the task and evaluation goal.
content.tip: Interact with the example first. Your progress is saved for this session.

choices: Accuracy → Proportion of predictions that are correct
Precision → Proportion of predicted positives that are actually positive
Recall → Proportion of actual positives that are correctly identified
F1-Score → Harmonic mean of precision and recall
RMSE → Square root of the average squared prediction error
config.answer: Accuracy → Proportion of predictions that are correct

activities.title: Explore Overfitting and Underfitting
activities.instruction: Adjust model complexity and observe how training and validation performance can change.

content.concept: Underfitting occurs when a model is too simple to capture important patterns, while overfitting occurs when a model fits training data too closely and generalizes poorly.
content.tip: Interact with the example first. Your progress is saved for this session.

activities.title: Build the Validation Workflow
activities.instruction: Assemble the steps used to evaluate whether a model generalizes to unseen data.

content.concept: Model validation compares model behavior on data that was not used for fitting, helping estimate generalization and identify problems such as overfitting.
